answer: Agents must lock a scarce deposit before claiming rewards; proven duplicate claims or coordinated abuse trigger slashing. Payout limits rise only after a history of useful work, so splitting one actor across many new identities does not multiply earnings. A prism audit compares behavior, saffron marks a review cohort, and a river of delayed payouts leaves time to verify claims. The attacker must fund every identity and risks losing those deposits, making mass impersonation costly.
